newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope saddened over Bernardin death.
newsitem.headline: Pope saddened over Bernardin death.

text.p: Pope John Paul said on Thursday that he was greatly saddened by the death of Chicago Cardinal Joseph Bernardin after a 16-month battle with cancer and praised the prelate's devotion to the Church.
In a message sent to the Chicago archdiocese, the 76-year-old Polish Pontiff said he had learned of the archbishop's death on Thursday morning "with great sadness".
He commended the cardinal's "noble soul" to God.
The Pope praised Bernardin's "untiring work" as priest, bishop and cardinal and as past general secretary and president of the U.S. Catholic Bishops Conference.
He spoke of Bernardin's dignity in the face of sufffering and death and hoped it would inspire all who knew him.

Bernardin, 68, the soft-spoken son of an Italian stone cutter, had talked by telephone in his final hours with both the Pope and President Bill Clinton. His death came a day before schoolchildren across the archdiocese were scheduled to assemble at special services to pray for him.
Raymond Flynn, the U.S. ambassador to the Vatican, said that with Bernardin's death, the United States and the Catholic Church had lost "one of their greatest moral leaders".

"Through his personal example, he taught us all the true meaning of the word 'courage'. This 'healing priest' was able to achieve greatness through his personal suffering and travails in the service of the Lord and the people, and he will leave an indelible mark on all of us," Flynn said in a statement.

In June 1995 Bernardin was found to be suffering from pancreatic cancer, a particularly deadly form of the disease, and underwent surgery. Last Aug. 30 he announced the disease had spread to his liver and was inoperable, giving him less than a year to live.
A few weeks ago he abandoned chemotherapy treatments.
